name: The Fall
label: Matador
lede: One man from Prestwich ran The Fall for 42 years, through 31 studio albums, 24 Peel sessions and roughly 60 musicians hired and fired, and stayed until the end.

eras.title: Camus, biscuit tins and the Sex Pistols
eras.text: Four friends from Prestwich and Salford saw the Sex Pistols and decided to make something stranger. Within two years half of them were gone, and Mark E. Smith's way of running a band was already set.

years.h: Four friends watch the Sex Pistols and decide to be stranger
years.p: On July 20, [[Mark E. Smith|35e5ce55-486d-40a4-9ab5-08de9be70d33]], [[Martin Bramah|d956f22a-27bf-45a0-9362-821eea53ddbb]], [[Una Baines|8afef734-a652-494e-b25e-0ff895fba38e]] and Tony Friel are at the Lesser Free Trade Hall in Manchester for the Sex Pistols. Friel names the band after Albert Camus's novel The Fall.
years.xp: Smith was a shipping clerk at the Salford docks at the time, after a first job in a meat factory. The four met to read each other's writing and take drugs. Baines couldn't afford a drum kit, so she played biscuit tins before switching to keyboards.

years.cap: The third line-up, c. 1977: Bramah, Baines, Burns, Friel and Smith
years.h: First gig: a basement, and a drummer nobody could name
years.p: The Fall's first show is in the North West Arts basement in Manchester. Writer Dave Simpson identified the drummer 34 years later: Steve Ormrod, who lasted one gig over politics.
years.xp: [[Karl Burns|4c79d249-fed7-4d8f-a05a-eeb96a6bdd02]], who had played with Friel in Nuclear Angel, took over on drums. That November, [[Buzzcocks|31e9c35b-2675-4632-8596-f9bd9286f6c8]] manager Richard Boon paid for the first recording session.

years.h: Friel walks out on Smith's girlfriend as manager
years.p: Kay Carroll, Smith's girlfriend, becomes the band's manager. Bassist Tony Friel doesn't like it, leaves, and forms The Passage.

years.h: Baines leaves after an overdose and a breakdown
years.p: Keyboardist Una Baines quits after a drug overdose and a nervous breakdown. Yvonne Pawlett takes her place.

years.h: A van driver's Hawaiian shirt costs the band its bassist
years.p: Eric McGann quits in disgust because driver Steve Davies wore one to the band's first [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] session. There would be 24 Peel sessions in all.
years.xp: Wikipedia puts it as McGann leaving "in disgust" over the shirt, worn while Davies ferried the band to the recording in May 1978.

years.h: The first record, Bingo-Master's Break-Out!, on Step Forward
years.p: The EP comes from the session [[Buzzcocks|31e9c35b-2675-4632-8596-f9bd9286f6c8]] manager Richard Boon paid for the previous November.

eras.title: Hip priests and two drummers
eras.text: A 16-year-old roadie became the bassist, and two players from a support band became the backbone for nearly two decades. The Fall made the records Peel played for the rest of his life, then Smith sacked the one member who fought back.

years.h: The 16-year-old roadie gets the bass
years.p: Marc Riley goes from carrying the gear to playing in the band. In April he moves to guitar.

years.h: One day in the studio, and then two members leave
years.p: The Fall cut Live at the Witch Trials in a single day in December 1978. Soon after it comes out, Bramah leaves to form [[Blue Orchids|62c562c9-f91d-4195-8924-86be20ab9d41]] with Baines, and Karl Burns quits.

years.h: Support band Staff 9 loses its guitarist and bassist to the Fall
years.p: Craig Scanlon and Steve Hanley come over together. Hanley's bass would define the sound for 19 years.

years.h: Cargo Studios worries Dragnet will put bands off
years.p: The Rochdale studio protested the murky sound of the album, worried it would put off other bands.

years.h: Paul Hanley, 16 and still at school, takes the drum stool
years.p: Drummer Mike Leigh quit for the cabaret circuit after weeks without work. Steve Hanley's younger brother Paul debuts at London's Electric Ballroom.

years.h: Grotesque tops the UK indie chart
years.p: The first album for Rough Trade after the live-and-rehearsal set Totale's Turns, on which Smith can be heard ordering drinks and berating the band.

q: a bunch of well-meaning but inept hippies
yt: Totally Wired, live in New York, June 1981
years.h: "Inept hippies" and a new label called Kamera
years.p: Smith leaves Rough Trade over its politics and signs with Kamera. Paul Hanley is too young for a US visa, so Burns returns for the tour and stays as a second drummer.
years.xp:
Wikipedia has Smith unhappy with Rough Trade's politics. The label put out the Slates EP in April 1981, and the band quit by the end of the year.

Smith's verdict on the people running it, in his own words: "a bunch of well-meaning but inept hippies."

years.src: Wikipedia: Hex Enduction Hour · Wikipedia: The Fall (band)
years.h: Lava-walled studios, two drummers and Hex Enduction Hour
years.p: Recorded in Reykjavik's Hljodriti and a disused cinema in Hitchin, and released March 8 on Kamera. HMV racked the crude cover backwards.
years.xp: It sold 20,000 copies by mid-1983. Its lyrics reportedly cost The Fall a Motown deal in 1984, and a piece of Hip Priest turns up in The Silence of the Lambs.

years.h: Smith sacks Riley, and Riley answers with Jumper Clown
years.p: After a run of rows, including a fistfight on the Australian tour, Smith fires him. Riley's new band The Creepers mocks Smith's clothes on the song.

eras.title: A Californian guitarist changes the sound
eras.text: A guitarist from California married Smith within three months of meeting him and pulled The Fall toward hooks. It was their most popular run, with covers in the UK charts and a ballet, and it ended in a divorce.

years.cap: Steve Hanley and Brix Smith on the Perverted by Language tour, Hamburg
years.h: Met at Chicago's Metro in April, married by July
years.p: Brix Smith meets Mark E. Smith on April 23 and marries him on July 19. Her first Fall gig is September 21 at the Hellfire Club in Wakefield.

years.h: Perverted by Language is Brix's first Fall album
years.p: Back on Rough Trade for one record. A live album from New Zealand, In a Hole, comes out on Flying Nun the same month.

years.h: Stolen gear sends both Hanleys out the door
years.p: Steve and Paul Hanley leave after the band's equipment is stolen. Steve is back midway through the next album.

years.h: Brix and Scanlon write the riffs for This Nation's Saving Grace
years.p: John Leckie produces on Beggars Banquet. [[LCD Soundsystem|2aaf7396-6ab8-40f3-9776-a41c42c8e26b]]'s James Murphy later called it formative.
years.xp: Simon Wolstencroft takes over as sole drummer afterwards, staying about 11 years.

years.h: A Motown cover gets the Fall to No. 30
years.p: There's a Ghost in My House, a cover of R. Dean Taylor's song, is their biggest hit so far. Victoria, a [[The Kinks|17b53d9f-5c63-4a09-a593-dde4608e0db9]] cover, reaches No. 35 in 1988.

years.h: I Am Kurious Oranj is music for a ballet
years.p: Written for a project with the dancer Michael Clark.

years.h: The marriage and the first Brix era end together
years.p: Brix Smith leaves the band and divorces Smith. Bramah returns for the next album, Extricate.

eras.title: Top ten, on Matador in America
eras.text: The Fall spent three albums on a major, then went back to indie labels in the UK while Matador Records put them out in the US. They scored their highest chart placing, got Brix back, and lost Scanlon.

years.h: No. 9 in the UK, and a Sister Sledge cover
years.p: The Infotainment Scan is the highest-charting album of their career, out on Permanent in the UK and Matador in the US. NME said it stood at the peak of their canon.

years.h: Karl Burns is back on drums, and Hey! Student places second in the Festive Fifty
years.p: Middle Class Revolt has Burns drumming on a Fall album for the first time since 1985. Covers include The Monks' Shut Up!.

years.h: Julia Nagle comes in, and the ex-wife returns
years.p: Nagle plays keyboards, guitar and computers. Brix Smith rejoins for Cerebral Caustic and The Light User Syndrome, then leaves again in 1996.

years.h: Sixteen years in, Craig Scanlon is sacked
years.p: Smith fires the guitarist after keyboardist Dave Bush joins [[Elastica|46693641-1e2e-4aae-80ed-6b28170de63a]]. He later said he regretted it.

years.h: Levitate flirts with drum and bass
years.p: Simon Wolstencroft quits mid-recording and Burns replaces him again. NME's Steven Wells gives the album a rave.

eras.title: Brownies, and after
eras.text: A New York show in 1998 ended with Smith arrested and the rhythm section gone for good. He rebuilt with whoever would stay, and by 2008 had a line-up that lasted to the end.

years.h: Brownies, New York: amps unplugged, a shove, an arrest
years.p: Smith's own account of the night he was arrested for assaulting Julia Nagle at the hotel, which he said was about sharing a room. It follows a last-night show where he unplugged the amps mid-song and Burns shoved him.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's account: onstage rows at Brownies, Smith unplugging the amps during songs and lashing out at the other members, Burns physically shoving him. Smith was arrested the next day and later called it "a heated argument" about sharing a room.

He was ordered into alcohol and anger-management treatment and the charges were later dropped. Nagle stayed in the band. Steve Hanley, after 19 years, left with Burns and guitarist Tommy Crooks, and told the story in his 2014 memoir The Big Midweek.

years.h: Smith and Nagle, with hired players
years.p: The pair rebuild The Fall for The Marshall Suite and, a year later, The Unutterable.

years.h: Elena Poulou, soon Smith's third wife, joins on keyboards
years.p: Q lists The Fall among its 50 Bands to See Before You Die.

yt: The Blindness, on Later with Jools Holland, 2005
years.h: BBC Four gives Smith an hour of his own
years.p: The Wonderful and Frightening World of Mark E Smith is a full documentary on him and the band. He also reads the classified football results on BBC's Final Score.

years.h: Four dates into a US tour, three members walk
years.p: The guitarist, bassist and drummer quit. Smith calls it the best thing that ever happened to the band.

years.h: Greenway, Spurr and Melling stay to the end
years.p: Pete Greenway, David Spurr and Keiron Melling play on Imperial Wax Solvent. Smith publishes his memoir, Renegade.

eras.title: The only constant
eras.text: The Fall finished on Domino and smaller labels with an album almost every year. Former members formed their own band, and Smith kept going until he couldn't stand.

years.h: Jeff Mangum books them for All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: [[Neutral Milk Hotel|a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75]]'s Mangum picks The Fall for the festival he curates at Minehead.

years.h: Brix and both Hanleys start Brix & the Extricated
years.p: Brix Smith Start, Steve Hanley and Paul Hanley form a band out of Fall veterans. Steve's memoir The Big Midweek comes out the same year.

years.h: Poulou resigns, and the marriage ends with it
years.p: Smith tells Mojo that Elena Poulou has quit after Sub-Lingual Tablet. They divorce the same year.

years.h: The 31st and last album, made as a four-piece
years.p: New Facts Emerge is the final studio album.

years.h: Smith's last show is at the Queen Margaret Union in Glasgow
years.p: The Fall's last show is on November 4. On November 29 in Bristol, Smith is too ill to leave his hotel and the band comes out to apologize.
years.xp: Wikipedia has the Bristol date at Fiddlers on November 29. It was cancelled because Smith couldn't leave the hotel.

eras.title: No Fall without Smith
eras.text: Smith's death ended The Fall on the spot; nobody discussed carrying on. What's left is the catalog, now with one label, and his leftover vocals.

years.cap: Mark E. Smith at SO36, Berlin
q: They are always different; they are always the same.
years.h: Mark E. Smith dies at home in Prestwich, aged 60
years.p: The cause is lung and kidney cancer after a long illness. He had been the only constant across about 60 musicians and 31 albums.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, falls in his later years had left him with bone fragmentation. His partner and manager when he died was Pamela Vander.

years.h: Cherry Red buys the rights to 40 Fall albums
years.p: The label announces a reissue series and a box set.

years.h: Post Script: the unused vocals, set to new music
years.p: Billed as a final album, it sets leftover Smith vocals to new backing by Simon 'Ding' Archer and Ed Blaney, who call it unheard recordings rather than a Fall studio album.
